abagtha.title: Abagtha
abagtha.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
abagtha.note: One of the seven eunuchs in Ahasuerus's household. His one appearance is being sent to fetch Queen Vashti so the king could show her off to his guests, which she refused to do.

abihail.title: Abihail
abihail.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
abihail.note: He appears twice in Esther, each time as somebody's father, and that is the whole of what the book does with him.

adalia.title: Adalia
adalia.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
adalia.note: One of Haman's ten sons. He was killed in Susa on the day that had been set for the Jews' destruction.

adar.title: Adar
adar.note: Twelfth month, late winter, and Purim falls in it, which is the whole reason Esther names it at all.

admatha.title: Admatha
admatha.about: Prince living at the time of Exile and Return
admatha.note: One of seven princes of Persia and Media who sat first in the kingdom and had access to the king. Ahasuerus consulted them after Queen Vashti refused to appear before him, and that is the only time his name comes up.

agagite.title: Agagite
agagite.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
agagite.note: What the book of Esther calls Haman, most likely marking him as a descendant of Agag, the Amalekite king Saul spared against God's command and Samuel then killed.

ahasuerus.title: Ahasuerus
ahasuerus.about: Emperor Xerxes I, living at the time of Exile and Return
ahasuerus.note: The Persian king who deposed Vashti and made Esther his queen. He is usually identified with Xerxes the First, whose reign is documented independently in Greek and Persian sources.

aridai.title: Aridai
aridai.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
aridai.note: Haman had ten sons, and he was one. The Jews of Susa killed them when they defended themselves against the slaughter Haman had planned. Nothing else is recorded of him.

aridatha.title: Aridatha
aridatha.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
aridatha.note: Another of Haman's ten sons, killed with his brothers on the day Haman had set for destroying the Jews, and his body was hanged afterwards.

arisai.title: Arisai
arisai.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
arisai.note: One more of the ten sons of Haman the Agagite, killed with his brothers in Esther 9 and named only in that list.

aspatha.title: Aspatha
aspatha.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
aspatha.note: Another of Haman's ten sons, killed after Haman's plot against the Jews fell apart.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

bigtha.title: Bigtha
bigtha.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
bigtha.note: One of King Ahasuerus's seven eunuchs, sent to bring Queen Vashti to the banquet. She refused. Nothing further is recorded about him.

bigthan.title: Bigthan
bigthan.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
bigthan.note: Bigthan and Teresh guarded the door of King Ahasuerus's chambers and plotted to kill him, and Mordecai found out and reported it.

biztha.title: Biztha
biztha.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
biztha.note: Another of the seven eunuchs at the court of Ahasuerus, likely Xerxes I, sent for Queen Vashti, who would not come.

carcas.title: Carcas
carcas.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
carcas.note: One of the seven eunuchs Ahasuerus sent to bring Queen Vashti before his guests, which she refused.

carshena.title: Carshena
carshena.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
carshena.note: He was one of the seven top princes of Persia and Media, advisers with direct access to King Ahasuerus. They were consulted after Queen Vashti refused to appear. Nothing further is recorded about him.

chush.title: Chush
chush.note: Cush as a land. It lay south of Egypt, roughly modern Sudan and Ethiopia, and the Old Testament keeps coming back to it as a distant, exotic country.

dalphon.title: Dalphon
dalphon.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
dalphon.note: The second of Haman's ten sons, killed by the Jews of Susa once his father's plot had failed.

esther.title: Esther
esther.about: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
esther.note: An orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai in Susa, she became queen when Ahasuerus put away his first wife. When Haman plotted to wipe out the Jews she went to the king uninvited, at the risk of her life, and Haman ended on his own gallows. The book never names God, and Purim still keeps the day.

hadassah.title: Hadassah
hadassah.about: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
hadassah.note: Esther's Hebrew name, before she took the Persian one she was known by as queen. She was an orphan, raised by her cousin Mordecai in Susa.

haman.title: Haman
haman.about: Persian living at the time of Exile and Return
haman.note: The Persian king's top official. Mordecai would not bow to him, and Haman's rage grew into a plot to kill every Jew in the empire on one day, until Queen Esther exposed it and he was hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai.

hammedatha.title: Hammedatha
hammedatha.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
hammedatha.note: Haman's father. Esther calls him the Agagite, which may tie the family to the old Amalekite royal line.

harbona.title: Harbona
harbona.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
harbona.note: One of the seven eunuchs of King Ahasuerus, sent to fetch Queen Vashti. At the end he points out the gallows Haman built for Mordecai, and Haman is hanged on it.

hatach.title: Hatach
hatach.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
hatach.note: Esther's eunuch, the go-between who carried her messages to Mordecai and back while Haman's plot hung over the Jews.

hegai.title: Hegai
hegai.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
hegai.note: The eunuch over King Ahasuerus's harem at Susa. He liked Esther from the start and gave her cosmetics, servants and the best place in the house, which likely helped her become queen.

india.title: India
india.note: Not a person. Esther marks the eastern edge of Ahasuerus's empire with it, with Cush at the other end and 127 provinces in between, and it most likely means the Indus region.

jair-4.title: Jair
jair-4.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
jair-4.note: A man from the exile and the return, and Esther is the only book that names him.

jeconiah.title: Jeconiah
jeconiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeconiah.note: Another name for Jehoiachin, the king of Judah carried off to Babylon. In the end a Babylonian king let him out and gave him a seat at the royal table.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jew.title: Jew
jew.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
jew.note: The word comes from Judah. At first it meant someone from the kingdom of Judah, and after the exile it came to cover the whole covenant people descended from Abraham, whatever tribe they came from.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kish-4.title: Kish
kish-4.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
kish-4.note: A man from the exile and the return, and Esther is the only book that names him.

madai.title: Madai
madai.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
madai.note: Japheth's son, and the ancestor of the Medes, who later joined Persia in taking Babylon.

marsena.title: Marsena
marsena.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
marsena.note: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media who advised Ahasuerus, men who could see the king and held the top seats in the kingdom.

mehuman.title: Mehuman
mehuman.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
mehuman.note: King Ahasuerus had seven eunuchs serving him, and Mehuman was one of those sent to fetch Queen Vashti for his guests, the order she refused at the start of Esther.

memucan.title: Memucan
memucan.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
memucan.note: When Queen Vashti refused the king's summons, Memucan was the adviser who said she should be put away, and that opened the door for Esther to become queen.

meres.title: Meres
meres.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
meres.note: One of the seven Persian princes close to Ahasuerus, consulted after Queen Vashti refused to come.

mordecai.title: Mordecai
mordecai.about: Esther's relative living at the time of Exile and Return
mordecai.note: A Benjamite in Susa who raised his orphaned cousin Esther as his daughter. He once exposed a plot to kill King Ahasuerus, and the king forgot it until a sleepless night had the records read to him. On the very day Haman had a gallows ready for him, Mordecai rode through the city in the king's robes, and he ended second in the empire.

nebuchadnezzar.title: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nebuchadnezzar.note: King of Babylon. He destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC and carried Judah off, and the Bible still calls him the tool God used to judge his people. Daniel tells how, after boasting of his greatness, he went mad and lived like an animal for seven years, until he gave God the glory and got his throne back.

nisan.title: Nisan
nisan.note: First month of the religious year, March into April. The older texts call it Abib, and Nehemiah and Esther both date by it.

parmasta.title: Parmasta
parmasta.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
parmasta.note: Haman had ten sons, and Parmashta was one of them, killed by the Jews of Susa on the day set for their own destruction.

parshandatha.title: Parshandatha
parshandatha.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
parshandatha.note: Haman's eldest son. He died with his nine brothers when the Jews of Susa defended themselves against the slaughter Haman had planned.

persia.title: Persia
persia.note: The empire that took Babylon under Cyrus. Unlike the empires before it, Persia let the exiled Jews go home and rebuild their temple, and Ezra keeps the decree.

poratha.title: Poratha
poratha.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
poratha.note: Haman had ten sons. Poratha was one, killed by the Jews of Susa when they defended themselves against the slaughter Haman had planned, and Purim remembers it.

pur.title: Pur
pur.note: It means a lot, the thing Haman cast to pick a date for killing the Jews. Purim takes its name from it, which reads like a joke at his expense.

shaashgaz.title: Shaashgaz
shaashgaz.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
shaashgaz.note: He was the eunuch over the king's concubines in the harem of Ahasuerus. Esther came under his charge after her first night with the king.

shethar.title: Shethar
shethar.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
shethar.note: One of the seven princes of Media and Persia who could go in to King Ahasuerus and advise him (Esther 1:14).

shimeah-15.title: Shimeah
shimeah-15.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
shimeah-15.note: A man from the exile and the return. Esther names him once.

shushan.title: Shushan
shushan.note: The Persian winter capital, east of the Tigris in what is now southwestern Iran, and the Greeks called it Susa. Most of the book of Esther happens here.

sivan.title: Sivan
sivan.note: Third month, May into June, and Esther dates the king's second decree to it.

tarshish-3.title: Tarshish
tarshish-3.about: Persian living at the time of Exile and Return
tarshish-3.note: A man from the exile and the return, and Esther is the only book that names him.

tebeth.title: Tebeth
tebeth.note: Tenth month, December into January, and the month Esther was taken in to the king.

teresh.title: Teresh
teresh.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
teresh.note: He and Bigthan guarded the door of King Ahasuerus and plotted to kill him. Mordecai found out and reported it, and both men were executed. The record of that service was later read to the king, and it turned the story of Esther.

vajezatha.title: Vajezatha
vajezatha.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
vajezatha.note: One of Haman's ten sons, killed when the Jews of Susa defended themselves on the day Haman had set for their destruction. Purim remembers it.

vashti-z.title: Vashti. z
vashti-z.about: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
vashti-z.note: Queen of Persia until she refused King Ahasuerus's order to come and be shown off to his banquet guests. He deposed her, and that opened the way for Esther.

zeresh.title: Zeresh
zeresh.about: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
zeresh.note: She was Haman's wife. She told him to build the gallows for Mordecai, and later, when things began to go wrong, told him he would fall before a Jew.

zethar.title: Zethar
zethar.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
zethar.note: One of the seven eunuchs King Ahasuerus sent to bring Queen Vashti before his guests. She refused, and that set off everything that led to Esther.
